reflection: Range-based cross-stock differences (NVDA range vs AAPL range) are the only kept signal; near copies and lags fail. Pure AAPL return/gap/position features fail. I will try other range/volatility comparisons with different constructions (e.g. high-low spreads of other peers, log-range ratios in windowed forms, true-range style) and new families like volume-range interaction and cross-stock volume ratios.

factors.name: nvda_range_vs_aapl_range_zscore_60
factors.hypothesis: Longer-window standardisation of the NVDA-vs-AAPL range gap captures relative stress regime shifts.

factors.name: nvda_range_vs_aapl_range_diff2
factors.hypothesis: Change in the relative range gap reflects shifting relative attention that may mean-revert in AAPL.

factors.name: nvda_qqq_range_avg_vs_aapl_range
factors.formula: subtract(multiply(add(safe_divide(subtract(NVDA_High, NVDA_Low), NVDA_Close), safe_divide(subtract(MSFT_High, MSFT_Low), MSFT_Close)), 0.5), safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_High, AAPL_Low), AAPL_Close))
factors.hypothesis: Average peer range (NVDA and MSFT) versus AAPL range gives a smoother relative-volatility signal.

factors.name: aapl_true_range_gap_vs_range
factors.hypothesis: Two-day range exceeding the one-day range signals gap-driven movement, informing next-day reversal or continuation.

factors.name: aapl_to_nvda_volume_ratio_log
factors.hypothesis: AAPL's abnormal volume relative to market abnormal volume flags stock-specific activity.

factors.name: nvda_abs_return_minus_aapl_abs_return
factors.hypothesis: Relative absolute move size between NVDA and AAPL proxies relative volatility regime that affects AAPL next-day direction.
